messages:
carla.sec: During today's RBAC sweep I found an unexpected external principal on the Vault transit wrapping key: partner-sync@thirdparty.iam.gserviceaccount.com. This was a console grant; tfstate has no record. We need a coordinated rotation + audit enablement.

matt.ops: thanks for flagging. paste the binding and any admin audit snippet?

carla.sec: binding snapshot:
- vault-service@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- svc-rewrap@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- partner-sync@thirdparty.iam.gserviceaccount.com  <-- unexpected

audit-bot: admin audit shows SetIamPolicy on 2026-03-22T02:14:07Z by admin@thirdparty.com. Note: KMS Data Access logs were NOT enabled for this keyRing.

iro.eng: OK. Proposed immediate steps: 1) remove external binding (record command) 2) create temporary wrapping key wrap-temp-<ts> with strict IAM (svc-rewrap + vault only) 3) enable KMS Data Access logs & create dedicated sink to security project 4) point Vault wrapping to temp key and run a single-object canary rewrap 5) full rewrap in maintenance window and rotate any SA keys that had access 6) bake key into terraform and add guardrail to block console SetIamPolicy on keyRings.

matt.ops: removal command (will run and paste output):
```
gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding wrap-key --location=global --keyring=transit --member='serviceAccount:partner-sync@thirdparty.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter'
```

carla.sec: do NOT disable old key until rewrap completes. we need to capture forensic evidence first (who accessed what).

vault-bot: Warning: transit/wrap-key currently used by mounts: backups, partner-credentials. 6 mounts report active wraps.

iro.eng: creating temp key now. rewrap canary plan (streaming decrypt->encrypt preserving metadata):
```
OBJ=gs://partner-archive/daily/2026-03-22/part-0001.bin.enc
# decrypt -> encrypt to new key, write .rewrap then move
gsutil cp "$OBJ" - | gcloud kms decrypt --location=global --keyring=transit --key=wrap-key --ciphertext-file=- --plaintext-file=- | gcloud kms encrypt --location=global --keyring=transit --key=wrap-temp-3533333210 --plaintext-file=- --ciphertext-file=- | gsutil cp - "$OBJ".rewrap && gsutil mv "$OBJ".rewrap "$OBJ"
```

matt.ops: enabling Data Access logs + sink now. sink command (audit-bot suggested):
```
gcloud logging sinks create sink-kms-data bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/redwood-security/datasets/kms_audit --log-filter='resource.type="crypto_key" AND protoPayload.methodName:"Encrypt"'
```

carla.sec: add a log-based alert to page sec on any future SetIamPolicy targeting keyRings: if matched -> page sec + oncall. we missed this console grant.

oncall: maintenance window available 01:00-03:00 UTC tonight. can do full rewrap then; I'll be operator. ping 15m before.

iro.eng: Vault change (canary): `vault write sys/wrapping/config wrap_key="projects/redwood-ops/locations/global/keyRings/transit/cryptoKeys/wrap-temp-3533333210"` — will deploy to vault-private canary pool first. rollback = repoint to old-key. monitor wrap success rate.

matt.ops: forensic query to list principals that used the keyring in last 30d (run now):
```
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_key_ring" protoPayload.methodName:"Encrypt" AND resource.labels.key_ring_name:transit' --freshness=30d --format='value(protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail)' | sort | uniq -c
```

carla.sec: if we see any external principals in encrypt/decrypt results, escalate to Legal & CISO immediately. Also snapshot checksums (crc32c/md5) before/after for canary objects.

iro.eng: temp key created: projects/redwood-ops/locations/global/keyRings/transit/cryptoKeys/wrap-temp-3533333210. opening terraform PR to make this managed and remove console drift possibility.

matt.ops: removed external binding and posted admin audit output here (no errors).

audit-bot: Incident INC-20260322-58 created. Tasks: remove binding (matt.ops) ✅, create temp key + canary (iro.eng) ✅, enable Data Access + sink (matt.ops) ✅, forensic timeline (carla.sec). Next update in 45m.

carla.sec: thanks team. remember to post exact commands and outputs in-thread so we have a single audit trace. I'll start the forensic timeline and post any suspicious downloads.
